hardware.variant: One assembled kit with operator-reported CoreBoard V1.2.

inputs.name: ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT RAM kernel with GPIO-bit-banged SPI and CO5300 framebuffer
inputs.revision: EmberBSD e2f027a9b6bfc86cbada9a8e24ff0cb4dfa8af5d; local FDT overrides disable hardware SPI and attach spigpio0 → spi0

scenario: RAM-boot ESP_MOSAICO_SC101IOT with local FDT overrides disabling hardware SPI and attaching spigpio0 to spi0. Request GPIO SPI at 100 kHz with spi-tx-bus-width=1; send ordinary pixel-write opcode 0x02 as a full-screen red fill. Do not send ALLPON and do not start LVGL.
expected: The initialized display shows the red console fill.
observed: The owner confirmed the display remained completely black. The kernel attached spigpio0 → spi0 → cofb0; GPIO SPI was requested at 100 kHz with a 100 kHz controller maximum. cofb0 reported rows_changed=960, rows_sent=960, errors=0 and last_error=0 after the 480-row initial refresh plus the 480-row red fill; the result stayed stable across four status reads. The transmit-only controller did not perform CO5300 status reads; attempts returned error 45 (EOPNOTSUPP). SC101IOT PID 0xda4a remained readable at SCCB address 0x68.
limits: One assembled V1.2 sample; this was a RAM-only trial and did not write NOR. The kernel FIT and static RAM root hashes identify the tested inputs.

The row counters cover the 480-row initial refresh and 480-row red fill and establish driver-reported transfer completion only. They do not establish whether the panel accepted the data or the state of its switched supply; no panel rail or electrical signal was measured.

A previous hardware-SPI trial also left the panel black. Together the two results mean SPI transport selection alone is not a sufficient explanation; neither trial proves panel command acceptance or rules out a transport fault.

No LVGL or ALLPON command was used in this trial. The sensor check establishes identity only; DVP capture is not implemented and this does not establish EmberBSD camera preview or operation of other modules.
The UART log and identifying device details remain private.
